note: State and territory facts the generator may state about worker screening, children's checks, restrictive practice authorisation and mandatory reporting (NDIS watch 13 October 2026, items A1, A2, A5, A7; batch 35, D-1801). Every fact carries its source and the day it was read; status verified means a state government, Commission or legislation page was read that day, unverified means a secondary summary. The prompt shows the provider's states only, and the model may not name a body or law that is not here.

ndisCheck.text: The NDIS Worker Screening Check is national: a clearance from any state or territory is valid across Australia for up to five years from the outcome date. The first clearances began expiring in February 2026; a renewal can be lodged up to 90 days before expiry, and a worker whose clearance has expired must be removed from risk-assessed roles immediately. Providers link each screened worker to their record in the NDIS Worker Screening Database and unlink workers who leave.

source.title: NDIS Commission, FAQs: NDIS Worker Screening Check renewal cycle (January 2026)

acceptableChecks.text: Every check s 14A(2) of the Worker Screening Rules names is a Part 4 transitional arrangement that has ended by its own date, so no acceptable state check applies today and the s 14A bar has no escape; s 29B ceased at the end of 1 February 2024 (s 29B(10)).

source.title: NDIS (Practice Standards—Worker Screening) Rules 2018, compilation No. 4, F2021C00788, s 14A(2) and Part 4 (currency confirmed on legislation.gov.au 15 October 2026)

workerScreening.text: NDIS Worker Check, applied for through Service NSW and assessed by the Office of the Children's Guardian; valid up to five years; separate from the Working With Children Check.

source.title: Service NSW, NDIS Worker Check

pendingWorkAllowed.text: New South Wales lets a worker start in a risk assessed role on a verified application: the Office of the Children's Guardian says arrangements are in place for a person to work while the application is assessed, once the NDIS employer has verified it in the NDIS Worker Screening Database, and the NSW Act itself requires no clearance and bars no work on a pending application (Part 2 note), save that those arrangements do not allow the work while an interim bar under s 9 is in force (s 9 note). Read by the PO 17 October 2026.

source.title: Office of the Children's Guardian, Application processing and employer verification; National Disability Insurance Scheme (Worker Checks) Act 2018 No 82 (NSW), Part 2 note and s 9, current version 23 September 2025 to date

applicationProhibitsPending.text: New South Wales does not prohibit work while a verified application is pending: the NSW Act requires no clearance of its own (Part 2 note: the requirement arises under the NDIS Act and the arrangements under the Intergovernmental Agreement) and the only bar is the Screening Agency's interim bar under s 9, which ends when revoked or when the application is granted or refused (s 9(4)). Read by the PO 17 October 2026.

source.title: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Worker Checks) Act 2018 No 82 (NSW), Part 2 note and s 9, current version 23 September 2025 to date; Office of the Children's Guardian, Application processing and employer verification

combinedScheme.text: In New South Wales the NDIS Worker Check and the Working With Children Check are two separate checks.

source.title: Service NSW, NDIS Worker Check

childrenCheck.text: Working With Children Check (WWCC) from the Office of the Children's Guardian; valid five years.

source.title: Service NSW, NDIS Worker Check

restrictivePractice.text: Restrictive practices are authorised by a Restrictive Practices Authorisation (RPA) Panel convened by the implementing provider under the Department of Communities and Justice RPA Policy; the framework is policy-based, not a statute; a senior manager may give an interim authorisation for up to six months.

source.title: NSW Department of Communities and Justice, Restrictive Practices Authorisation portal

workerScreening.text: NDIS Worker Screening Check from the NDIS Worker Screening Unit, applied for through Service Victoria; valid up to five years; it does not replace the Working with Children Check.

source.title: Victorian Government, NDIS Worker Screening Check

pendingWorkAllowed.text: Victoria: no clearance, no start. A worker may not begin in a risk assessed role until the clearance is issued.

source.title: Victorian Government, NDIS Worker Screening Check

applicationProhibitsPending.text: Victoria prohibits work in a risk assessed role until the clearance is issued: no clearance, no start.

source.title: Victorian Government, NDIS Worker Screening Check

combinedScheme.text: In Victoria the NDIS Worker Screening Check and the Working with Children Check are two separate checks.

source.title: Victorian Government, NDIS Worker Screening Check

childrenCheck.text: Working with Children Check from the Social Services Regulator; valid five years. From 19 October 2026 an applicant must complete the free WWC Child Safety Training before applying.

source.title: Victorian Government, Working with Children Check

restrictivePractice.text: Restrictive practices are authorised under the Disability Act 2006 (Vic) Part 7 as amended in 2023: the provider's Authorised Program Officer for chemical and environmental restraint, and the Victorian Senior Practitioner (Department of Families, Fairness and Housing) for seclusion, physical and mechanical restraint.

source.title: Department of Families, Fairness and Housing, Victorian Senior Practitioner

workerScreening.text: NDIS worker screening clearance from Worker Screening Queensland (Disability Worker Screening); it can be applied for together with the Blue Card as one combined application; valid up to five years. Record the NDIS clearance number and expiry separately from the Blue Card.

source.title: Worker Screening Queensland, fees for workers

pendingWorkAllowed.text: Queensland: a worker can't start work until they have been issued a clearance, and employers must verify the engagement before the application is considered valid.

source.title: Worker Screening Queensland, before you start

applicationProhibitsPending.text: Queensland prohibits work in a risk assessed role until the clearance is issued.

source.title: Worker Screening Queensland, before you start

combinedScheme.text: In Queensland the NDIS clearance and the Blue Card are one combined application with one fee; the two clearances are still recorded separately.

source.title: Worker Screening Queensland, before you start

childrenCheck.text: Blue Card from Blue Card Services; valid three years.

source.title: Worker Screening Queensland, fees for workers

restrictivePractice.text: Restrictive practices are authorised under the Disability Services Act 2006 (Qld): short-term approvals from the Department of Families, Seniors, Disability Services and Child Safety; the Public Guardian and QCAT for containment and seclusion.

source.title: Queensland Department of Families, Seniors, Disability Services and Child Safety, positive behaviour support and restrictive practices resources

pendingWorkAllowed.text: Western Australia allows a worker to start on a complete, verified application with no interim bar in place.

applicationProhibitsPending.text: Western Australia does not prohibit work on a complete, verified application with no interim bar.

childrenCheck.text: Working with Children Check from the Department of Communities; valid three years.

source.title: WA Department of Communities, authorisation of restrictive practices

childrenCheck.text: Working With Children Check from the Department of Human Services Screening Unit; valid five years.

restrictivePractice.text: Restrictive practices are authorised under the Disability Inclusion Act 2018 (SA) Part 6A: the Senior Authorising Officer in the Restrictive Practices Unit, with provider Authorised Program Officers for level 1 practices; an interim authorisation lasts up to 8 months and a comprehensive one up to 15.

source.title: SA Government, Restrictive Practices Unit; restrictive practices authorisation frameworks table

workerScreening.text: The NDIS clearance is issued inside Registration to Work with Vulnerable People (RWVP) from the Department of Justice; valid up to five years or for the registration term. Record the NDIS clearance number and expiry separately from the registration card.

source.title: Tasmanian Department of Justice, RWVP: NDIS worker check

pendingWorkAllowed.text: Tasmania's page is silent on pending work; the database asks the employer to verify the application.

source.title: Tasmanian Department of Justice, RWVP: NDIS worker check

applicationProhibitsPending.text: Tasmania's page is silent on whether an applicant may work while the application is pending.

source.title: Tasmanian Department of Justice, RWVP: NDIS worker check

combinedScheme.text: In Tasmania one Registration to Work with Vulnerable People carries the NDIS check, requested as part of the application, valid for 5 years or the duration of the registration.

source.title: Tasmanian Department of Justice, RWVP: NDIS worker check

childrenCheck.text: Registration to Work with Vulnerable People (child-related) from the Department of Justice; valid five years.

source.title: Tasmanian Department of Justice, RWVP: NDIS worker check

restrictivePractice.text: Restrictive practices are authorised by the Senior Practitioner in the Department of Premier and Cabinet under the Disability Rights, Inclusion and Safeguarding Act 2024 (Tas), in force from 1 July 2025, which replaced TASCAT approvals under the 2011 Act; an authorisation lasts up to 12 months.

source.title: TASCAT, changes to restrictive intervention applications

workerScreening.text: The NDIS clearance is issued on the Working with Vulnerable People (WWVP) registration from Access Canberra; valid five years when applied for together, otherwise it expires with the WWVP registration. Record the NDIS clearance number and expiry separately from the registration card.

restrictivePractice.text: Restrictive practices are authorised under the Senior Practitioner Act 2018 (ACT): a positive behaviour support plan is approved by a panel and registered with the ACT Senior Practitioner; a registration lapses after 12 months.

source.title: SAFE NT, NDIS Worker Screening Check

restrictivePractice.text: Restrictive practices are authorised by the NT Senior Practitioner in the Department of Health under the NT Restrictive Practices Authorisation Framework and the NDIS (Authorisations) Act 2019 (NT).

source.title: NT Department of Health, restrictive practices authorisation

part4Ends.text: The latest day a Part 4 arrangement under s 14(1)(b) could run to, per state, by the Rules' own years; Queensland's depends on the card held at 31 January 2021 and is unverified until the yellow card's term is read; Victoria's s 25(5)(d)(iii) has no end date in the text and is unverified (SR-5).

source.title: NDIS (Practice Standards—Worker Screening) Rules 2018, compilation No. 4, F2021C00788, Part 4 ss 23 to 29B
